title: Equal completeness gave no clear change in moth richness warmth slopes in four British samples in 1992-2015
abstract: We compared moth richness at 90 percent estimated sample completeness with richness at 100 individuals. Four samples covered England and Scotland in 1992-2003 and 2004-2015. The comparison retained 548 of 685 eligible trap-months from a prior campaign panel. Direct warmth-slope differences were +0.796 and +0.500 taxa per C in England and +0.447 and +0.421 in Scotland. All four corrected intervals included zero. One completeness slope was positive, but its direct contrast was uncertain. Targets of 80 and 95 percent and two model checks also gave uncertain direct contrasts. Equal size did not give equal completeness. Requiring completeness removed 20 percent of eligible months. Selected samples, few Scottish sites, coarse weather and capture bias limit inference. This study uses the same biological records as prior campaign work. It tests a new measurement comparison, not a causal climate or pollution effect. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, checks and a figure are included. External record-level data stay outside the publication.

display.caption: Warmth slopes at fixed size and fixed estimated completeness, and their direct differences. Intervals correct for four country-period tests within each outcome. All direct difference intervals include zero.
